titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 16/2014 (ޖިންސީ ފުރައްސާރަކުރުމާއި ގޯނާކުރުން ހުއްޓުވުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the 2014 law on preventing sexual harassment and abuse, mainly the duties of workplaces. Every employer would have to write and publish an anti-sexual-harassment policy. Employers would have to train staff, handle complaints according to that policy, protect complainants and witnesses, and appoint a compliance officer. The bill also changes how complaints are investigated and the penalties employers face. This summary covers only the first 12 of 42 pages.
whyItMatters: Anyone who works would get clearer protection and a set process for reporting harassment at work. Employers of all sizes would take on new legal duties.
keyProvisions: Replaces Article 7: every employer must prepare and publish a sexual harassment prevention policy covering its purpose, what counts as harassment, how to complain, how complaints are investigated, disciplinary steps and confidentiality.
Replaces Article 8: employers must inform and train staff on the law and policy, handle complaints under the policy, act when harassment happens, and review the policy regularly.
New Article 8-1: employers must appoint a compliance officer to advise on the law, help draft the policy, run awareness work and keep records of complaints.
Article 18 amendments: investigations of sexual harassment complaints are to be completed within 3 months.
Amends Articles 10, 14 and 17 on employer liability, what the enforcing authority can do, and fines (details only partly read).
whoIsAffected: Employees and employers in every workplace, and the authority that enforces the 2014 law.
statedReasons: The government says the bill strengthens how Law 16/2014 prevents sexual harassment and abuse in workplaces. It does this by setting clearer duties for employers and better ways to handle complaints.
